Class UnprocessedRequestException

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Throwable
java.lang.Exception
java.lang.RuntimeException
io.micronaut.http.exceptions.HttpException
io.micronaut.http.client.exceptions.HttpClientException
io.micronaut.http.client.exceptions.UnprocessedRequestException
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class UnprocessedRequestException extends HttpClientException
The request was not sent: no byte of it reached the server, so the server did not process it. Such a request can be sent again, whatever its method and body, without the server seeing it twice, which is what a retry of a non-idempotent request needs to know. The UnprocessedRequestException.Reason says why it was not sent.

NoAvailableServiceException, thrown when the load balancer has no instance to send the request to, is the other exception of a request that was not sent: isUnprocessed(Throwable) covers both.

getUri() and getServiceInstance() name the server the request was for, when known, e.g. to exclude it from the next attempt.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov
